name: AR-04
label: Safe R

model.rationale: The R+20 lean, Westerman's overwhelming financial advantage, and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at 3% all point to a safe Republican hold; the challenger's negligible fundraising rules out a serious race.
model.watch: Only a major unforeseen scandal or national wave of historic size could put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bruce Westerman, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win re-election in this southern Arkansas district. The seat leans Republican by about 20 points, and Westerman enters the general election with roughly $4.7 million on hand after raising more than $2.5 million. His Democratic opponent, James Russell, has raised under $6,000 and reported only about $900 in cash, leaving him with no visible resources to compete. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 3% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the financial imbalance, and market pricing. The expected margin is about 19 points Republican, with modest uncertainty given how lopsided the fundamentals are. Any surprise would require an extraordinary external shock rather than campaign dynamics within the district.
